solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Lowers temperature, repeatedly dipping in cold beer

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: the repeated letter dips into the drink, so it sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: the temperature abbreviation is used twice over in this clue

explanation.surface: Someone chills their cold beer by dunking things in it again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lowers' reads as a verb meaning reduces, but it is a noun: animals that low, as cows do.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows and oxen make a lowing noise, so the herd can be called lowers in a playful noun sense.

clue.text: Succeed with appeal? Do be sensible!

parts.note: a plan that comes off succeeds
it means sex appeal, as in the 1927 film It

explanation.surface: Someone tells a hopeful applicant to be realistic about winning an appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom is a scornful request to stop pretending or talking nonsense, i.e. be sensible.

clue.text: This is spoken for all we know by part-time soldiers

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the two pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's former part-time reserve force
one's ken is the range of one's knowledge

explanation.surface: Part-time soldiers say something is spoken for, as far as they know.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat or a person already reserved or committed is said to be spoken for.

clue.text: As an expert viewer, join team for broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the airwaves, so the words are heard, not read

parts.note: link means join, and side means team

explanation.surface: An expert viewer is invited to join a team for a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'join team' gives LINK SIDE, which said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lynx were believed to have exceptional sight, so the term means keen-sighted.

clue.text: Dry clothing rushed round hospital's parts

indicators.note: the teetotal letters dress or wrap around the reversed piece

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, i.e. dry

indicators.note: turned round means the word for rushed is read backwards

parts.note: flew means hurried or rushed
H is the abbreviation for hospital, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Something dry is wrapped around rushing parts of a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' is the teetotal abbreviation, and 'round' turns the word for rushed back to front before the teetotal letters wrap it.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelfths are fractions, each one a part of a whole divided into twelve equal shares.

clue.text: Stew fresh meat on one side

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next
fresh suggests something made anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ham is a meat
united means as one

explanation.surface: A recipe: stew some fresh meat on one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' looks like the side of a pan; it is a football team. WEST HAM UNITED is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a side is a team, and this is a London Premier League club.

clue.text: Scottish town has large area with grass

parts.note: a grass and a nark are both slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: A Scottish town boasts a large area of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is British slang for an informer, as is NARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanark is a town in South Lanarkshire, Scotland.

clue.text: After working, relish a TV play

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: After work, someone settles down to enjoy a play on TV.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rivals is a comedy of manners by Richard Brinsley Sheridan, first staged in 1775.

clue.text: Girl succeeded with exploit, enthralling one

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: to use someone is to exploit them
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl succeeds by exploiting someone she has under her spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Susie is a girl's name, a pet form of Susan.

clue.text: Heavens opening for karaoke on unusually large holiday island

parts.note: my! and heavens! are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size for the unusually large

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims about karaoke being on a huge scale on a holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: Mykonos is a Greek island in the Cyclades, a popular holiday and party destination.

clue.text: Playing fairly unusual part involving some links

indicators.note: unusual suggests things out of their normal order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer plays fair in an unusual round that takes in some links courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' and 'some links' are anagrammed together; 'involving' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving with fairness and good grace in a game describes a sportsman's ideal conduct.

clue.text: Offering nothing for a tanner daily? Not so!

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper
less means not so much, as in less happy = not so happy

explanation.surface: A sunbather finds nothing on offer from a daily paper, but says otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tanner' is a sunbather here, not the old British sixpence coin it can also mean.
explanation.definitionFit: A day without sunshine gives a sunbather no chance of getting a tan.

clue.text: Wildcat strike abandoned by leader

indicators.note: the word loses its leading letter, which leaves it

parts.note: to pounce is to strike suddenly, as a cat does

explanation.surface: A wildcat strike is called off by the union leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wildcat strike' looks like an industrial dispute; the definition is 'Wildcat' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard of Central Asia is also called by this name, a large wild feline.

clue.text: Different books of the Bible present short description of Solomon

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of the Bible's books

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: here means present, in attendance
King Solomon is proverbially wise

explanation.surface: Books of the Bible offer a brief and unusual portrait of King Solomon.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective this word means unlike or other than, as in 'quite the reverse of what was thought'.

clue.text: Overweight lady's against me wanting an hourglass figure

parts.note: fat means overweight
her refers to a lady; the possessive gives no letter

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letters of the following word are removed

parts.note: anti means against
the word an is the letters removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heavy woman complains about a rival who has the coveted hourglass figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hourglass figure' suggests a curvy body; it is the personified old man who carries an hourglass. 'wanting' removes AN from ANTIME, leaving TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Time personified is pictured as a bearded old man holding a scythe and an hourglass.

clue.text: Wearing headdress with raised dull pattern forbidden

indicators.note: raised means turned upwards, so in a down clue the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine pattern of life
banned means forbidden

explanation.surface: Wearing a headdress with a raised dull pattern is banned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing a turban, a wound cloth headdress, is described this way.

clue.text: Stick note in bundle

indicators.note: the note's letter goes inside the bundle word

parts.note: a wad is a bundle, as of banknotes

explanation.surface: Someone sticks a note into a bundle of papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A magician's or conductor's slender rod is a thin stick.

clue.text: Bureau I left guided with a lower degree of expertise

definitions.text: with a lower degree of expertise

parts.note: a bureau is a writing desk
led means guided

explanation.surface: An office worker left a bureau, guided by someone less expert.
explanation.definitionFit: When a job is deskilled it requires less skill, so the workers need less expertise.

clue.text: Rookie private supporting request with humility

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: to beg is to ask humbly
inner means private, as in one's inner thoughts

explanation.surface: A rookie private soldier humbly backs a request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like a soldier; it is the adjective, INNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a newcomer or novice, someone just starting out.

clue.text: Patch half Ruth's back pockets

indicators.note: back means the run of letters is read in reverse
the phrase pockets, holding inside it, the letters needed

explanation.surface: Someone sews a patch onto half of Ruth's back pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pockets' signals letters held inside 'half Ruth's', giving FRUT; 'back' then turns it round. 'half' is not a halving instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: One's turf or patch is the area one regards as one's own territory.

clue.text: Renegade UN names as one who may work with dictator?

indicators.note: renegade suggests going astray, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rebel group renames a United Nations official who works with a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dictator' suggests a tyrant; it is someone dictating letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretary or scribe who takes down what someone says aloud works for a person dictating.

clue.text: Wine taster's gift a year overdue

parts.note: PA is per annum, a year
late means overdue

explanation.surface: A present of wine for a taster arrives a year late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gift' is not a present but a talent: a wine taster's sense of taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A discerning sense of taste is the natural talent a wine expert relies on.

clue.text: Concealing advances, leave at disadvantage

parts.note: to go is to leave

indicators.note: concealing means the outer pair of words hide the other piece inside them

parts.note: gains are advances, as in making progress

explanation.surface: Someone hides their progress, leaving a rival at a disadvantage.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unfavourable to someone, as when a verdict works against them, is the same as to put them at a disadvantage.

clue.text: Mouth with a bit of puff that's become putrid

parts.note: gob is slang for mouth
puff is promotional hype, and an ad is one piece of it

explanation.surface: A mouth breathes in a puff of something rotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that spoils or rots is said to turn or go off, i.e. turn rotten.

clue.text: A medical professional getting one on one's feet

indicators.note: in an across clue the first group of letters is placed on, i.e. after, the other

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one; the possessive gives no letter
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A doctor gets a patient back on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feet' looks like the patient's feet; they are metrical feet in verse. A + MB + I is placed after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambs, plural of the Latin form, are metrical feet of one short and one long syllable.

clue.text: Cram receptacle in pub with excellent spirits

parts.note: a mug is a drinking vessel, as for beer in a pub
up means in high spirits, cheerful

explanation.surface: Someone crams a mug in the pub with spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' suggests drink; it is a mood, being UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise intensively for an exam is British slang for cramming.

clue.text: Tongue wagging began with short fib

indicators.note: wagging means the letters move about and are rearranged
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a lie is a fib

explanation.surface: Someone's tongue began wagging and they told a little fib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue wagging' reads as gossip, but 'Tongue' is the definition: a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the language of Bangladesh and West Bengal, and a tongue is a language.

clue.text: Irish town I miss after departure to the far west

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come after the first letter
the leftmost, most westerly, letter of the word is taken

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a gal is a girl, a miss

explanation.surface: An Irish town that someone misses after leaving it for the far west.
explanation.definitionFit: Donegal is a town in the far northwest of Ireland, giving its name to the county.

clue.text: Trot back to collect stranger, one unsteady on his feet

indicators.note: the reversed word collects, holding inside it, the other piece
back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a Trot (Trotskyist) is a red, a left-winger
odder means stranger

explanation.surface: Someone trots back to collect a stranger who is wobbly on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trot' is not a gait but a Trotskyist, a RED; 'back' makes DER, which holds ODDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who totters about shakily, usually from old age, is unsteady on their feet.

clue.text: Stand one effect of drug overdose

parts.note: a trip is the hallucinatory experience from a drug like LSD

explanation.surface: Someone takes a stand on the effects of a drug overdose.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged support for a camera or telescope is a kind of stand.
